ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A lifeline is the thread by which life continues. Chan records apply the word to the continuity of the buddhas and patriarchs, to what can be transmitted through a qualified person, and to the vital point Yunwai Xingze says an old case exposes in the hearers themselves.
EvidenceBody: The Blue Cliff Record preface calls its subject the sages’ lifeline and the patriarchs’ great working, placing the word in the transmission of the public record.
Yinyuan Longqi says that if such a person appears, the buddhas’ and patriarchs’ lifeline can be transmitted; without one, he will go into the mud and water himself.
Yunwai Ze says the patriarch has “pointed out your lifeline” and immediately warns that adding another explanatory phrase merely returns the hearers to sleep.
Jiqi Hongchu asks for someone able to act as the eyes of humans and gods at the patriarch’s lifeline. The image names continuity and the exposed vital point, not a biological organ.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Chan bends a bodily vital line into the transmissible continuity and immediately exposed vital point of the ancestral record.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The word does not name a separately defined substance; each occurrence identifies whose continuity or vital point is at stake.

ComparedThings: The sages’ lifeline, the patriarchs’ lifeline, and a hearer’s exposed lifeline use one vital-thread image
DifferentThingTest.Reason: The sages’ lifeline, the patriarchs’ lifeline, and a hearer’s exposed lifeline use one vital-thread image. Possessor and scale change, but no passage identifies a separate anatomical vessel.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Lifeline, vital thread, lineage, patriarchal, and your own reflect the corpus’s changing possessors while keeping one English image.

ModifierControls.reason: 命根 and 續命脈 were checked as relatives: 命根 is a life-root and 續 is the act of continuing the same lifeline; neither licenses merging their entries.

FamilyControls.reason: 佛祖命脈, 祖師命脈, and 諸人命脈 show institutional, ancestral, and directly addressed possessors of the same image rather than master-specific senses.
